headline.purpose: The one title a panel may carry: search form heading, setup and offline stages.

title.purpose: The name of the thing in a detail panel: item name, picker heading, results count.

section.purpose: Group headings inside a panel: stat categories, Effects, Conditions, Set.

body.purpose: Sentences, effect lines and row text; supporting sentences in ink-2.

data.purpose: Values: bold, tabular, right-aligned in columns.

label.purpose: Field labels, table headers, the second line under an item name.

numeral.purpose: The four vital figures of a stuff (HP, AP, MP, range) and nothing else.

shadows.name: shadow-pop
shadows.purpose: The only shadow: popovers, menus, select lists, toasts, the item sheet when it overlays the table, and the builder's picker as a bottom sheet.

shadows.name: slot-ring
shadows.purpose: State outline of the selected slot (red when the slot is also invalid). Not elevation.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve for every state transition.

motion.name: control
motion.purpose: Buttons, chips, slots, inputs, popup fade and scale.

motion.name: drop-in

narrative.namingNote: Naming note: the North Star and the descriptive colour names in this file (Range Blue, Movement Green, Impact Red, Board Sage and the rest) were derived from the build's direction contract. The user has not confirmed them yet; the token names in `styles.css` are the stable reference.
narrative.overview:
The interface borrows the surface a Dofus player already stares at in a fight: a tinted ground laid out in a two-tone checker, square cells, and the three zone colours the game uses to say what a cell means. Blue is where the player's hand is (the game's spell range), green is what is valid (movement), red is what fails (impact). Characteristics are read in the colour of their element. Nothing else on the screen carries hue, so every colour a player sees is information they already know how to read.

It is a working tool, dense on purpose. The root size is small (14px), rows are fixed and compact, numbers are tabular and bold, and labels step back to a softer ink so that values are what the eye lands on. The three screens share one frame: a top strip with the three destinations and the data release, then columns that fill the window and scroll on their own. There is no page chrome, no hero, no marketing voice.

It refuses two looks by construction: the dark neon gamer dashboard (no glow, no gradients on controls, the dark theme is the same sage board at night, not black) and the white SaaS admin table (the ground is tinted, state is carried by game colours, item cells and slots are the recurring shape instead of cards).

Tokens live in one place, `packages/app/src/styles.css`: the light theme on `:root`, the dark theme on `:root[data-theme="dark"]`. That file is normative. The frontmatter above is the light theme as it stood when this was written; if a value there and the stylesheet disagree, the stylesheet is right and the role described here still holds.
keyCharacteristics: A sage board ground in both themes: plain under the rails that hold controls, in a two-tone checker wherever pieces are placed or nothing has been picked or asked yet.
Square cells for every item image and every equipment slot, in three sizes of the same shape.
Three zone colours used only as state: blue selected, green valid, red failing.
Twelve stat tones, resolved from the stat itself, shown as a cell-shaped pip or as the colour of the number.
One typeface, four weights, tabular numerals everywhere.
Flat panels separated by one-pixel lines; shadow only under things that float.
Light and dark themes with the same roles; both are first-class.

rules.name: The Zone Colour Rule
rules.body: Blue, green and red are states, never decoration. Blue says "this is selected, or this is the move"; green says "this passes"; red says "this fails or is negative". A surface that is none of those stays neutral.

rules.name: The Soft-Fill Rule
rules.body: State on a surface is the soft wash as fill, with the strong colour kept for the border, the icon or a two-pixel ring; text on a wash stays ink. The strong colour is used as a fill only where blue means "pressed" or "do it" (solid button, pressed chip).

rules.name: The Element Rule
rules.body: A stat's colour is decided by the stat, in one function. No screen assigns a stat colour locally, and a tone is applied only to a pip or to the number itself, never to a panel, a border or a button. A mark that is not a stat (the update dot) gets its own tone name instead of borrowing a stat's.

rules.name: The State Never Rides On Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every zone colour arrives with a second signal: a tick, cross or warning icon, a status word, a ring. A stuff is never shown valid by default; the mark appears only once the evaluation says so.

rules.name: The Numbers First Rule
rules.body: In any label-and-value pair the value is bold ink and the label is `ink-2`. A zero drops to weight 500 and `ink-3` so non-zero values stand out in a long sheet.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Tabular numerals are on for the whole document. Numeric columns are right-aligned; names are left-aligned and truncate with an ellipsis rather than wrap.

rules.name: The Four Weights Rule
rules.body: 400 for prose, 600 for labels and controls, 700 for values and titles, 800 for vitals. No italics, no tracked uppercase labels, no letter-spacing other than a slight tightening on the product name.

rules.name: The Ground Rule
rules.body: The ground is for rails, stages and empty states; data sits on `panel`. Plain `ground` is the filter rail. The checker is where pieces are placed or where nothing is there yet: the builder's board, the item-sheet column before an item is picked, the setup and offline stages, the first load, the search screen before a run. Tables, lists and sheets sit on `panel`, edge to edge, with no ground showing between their rows.

rules.name: The Why-It-Matches Rule
rules.body: A stat the player filters on always gets a column in the table, so the reason a row is there is visible.

rules.name: The Flat Board Rule
rules.body: Nothing resting on the frame casts a shadow. If it does not float over other content, it gets a line, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Square Cell Rule
rules.body: Anything that is an item, a slot or a stat marker is a square cell. Item art never appears in a circle, a bare image or a card.

rules.name: The Pip Rule
rules.body: A characteristic is marked by one pip in its tone, never by a pictogram. The pip sits before the label; the label still names the stat. A stat with no tone keeps a hollow pip, so the column stays aligned without inventing a colour.

dos: Do take every colour from the tokens in `styles.css` and define both themes when adding one.
Do resolve a stat's colour through `toneOf` and show it as a pip or as the number's colour.
Do pair every zone colour with an icon, a word or a ring, and keep text on a wash in ink.
Do put item art in a square cell at one of the existing sizes, with the slot glyph as its fallback.
Do keep values bold and right-aligned, labels in `ink-2`, and zero values quiet.
Do keep one solid blue button per panel; everything else is default or ghost.
Do separate panels with one-pixel lines and let each column scroll on its own.
Do keep the ground for rails, stages and empty states: plain under a rail of controls, checker behind slots and wherever nothing has been picked or asked yet.
Do put item art on `cell-bg` or `slot-bg`, never straight on a panel, so dark art stays readable in the dark theme.
Do give a mark that is not a stat its own tone name, and keep set markers outside the blue, green and red state hues.
donts: Don't use `accent`, `ok` or `bad` to decorate; if a surface is not selected, valid or failing, it stays neutral.
Don't apply a stat tone to a panel, border or button, and don't give a stat a colour outside the tone map.
Don't replace pips with stat pictograms, or item cells with circles, bare images or cards.
Don't add shadows to panels, rows or cells; only floating layers cast one.
Don't add glow, gradient fills on buttons, panels or text, or a black neon dark theme; the dark ground is the same sage, at night.
Don't lay data tables, lists or sheets on the ground or the checker, or box result rows into cards.
Don't show a stuff as valid before its evaluation says so, or hide a failing condition behind colour alone.
Don't introduce a second typeface, tracked uppercase labels, or weights outside the four in use (a quiet zero at 500 is the one exception).
